answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the glacier schedule in the reef ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the summit checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 236 aliases thus means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. That is 32 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
